title: Nemi's resolve
hook: a good king is shown where actions lead, then goes home to govern well
tomorrow: what's the one thing you keep calling someday?

segments.voice: A week of three perfections. Patience: patient under wrong, no complaints. Truth: true, true under pressure, exactly true. And yesterday, resolve: decide once, then come back to it.
screen: `PATIENT UNDER WRONG · NO COMPLAINTS` → `TRUE · TRUE UNDER PRESSURE · EXACTLY TRUE` → `RESOLVE`

segments.voice: A crash video in driver's ed. A tour of a hospital ward. Sometimes one look at where things end up changes how a person drives home. The Jataka has a king who gets that look. King Nemi is good already: generous, keeping the precepts. Then, the story says, Sakka, king of the gods, sends his charioteer Matali to carry Nemi up to see the hells and the heavens.
screen: `ONE LOOK AT WHERE IT ENDS UP.` → `A GOOD KING, ALREADY.` → `A CHARIOT TO SEE IT ALL.`

segments.voice: Matali drives him first past the hells, where the story shows the fruit of cruelty and greed, and then through the heavens, where it shows the fruit of giving and keeping one's word. At each stop Nemi asks what these beings did. Then he's offered a place in heaven, and he turns it down. He'd rather do good himself, he says, than live on a gift. He goes home to govern well, to keep giving and keeping the precepts, because now he has seen, plainly, where actions lead. He resolved. The tour isn't there to frighten him into goodness; he was good already. It shows him that ordinary choices matter, and that turns a good habit into a resolve. Notice how the week sits inside the story. Patience for the long work of ruling. Truth heard without flinching. And a vision that didn't turn into fear. It turned into resolve, and the resolve turned into ordinary days of good rule.
screen: `FIRST THE HELLS, THEN THE HEAVENS.` · `WHAT DID THESE BEINGS DO?` · `NO THANKS: HE GOES HOME.` · then, large: `HE RESOLVED.`

segments.voice: Take a slow sip of water or tea and taste it all the way down. As you swallow, name the one thing you resolved yesterday. Let each sip during the sit be a small return to it.
Nemi's resolve: a good king sees where actions lead, and goes home resolved to govern well.
Something to keep: he resolved, saw where it leads, then went home and kept doing good. Two weeks, done.

howItsDone: The Nemi (Nimi) Jataka is one of the last ten Jataka tales, tied by tradition to the perfection of resolve; its tour of the heavens and hells is a common subject of Theravada temple murals and sermons.

fork.setup: after a scary near-miss on the highway, your friend says she'll never drive again. what would Nemi's story suggest?
options: let the scare become resolve: drive more carefully, starting now.
stop driving for good; you've seen where it can lead.
forget it fast; dwelling on it only makes you nervous.
fork.reveal: Nemi saw where actions lead and didn't hide from it or forget it. he went home and lived it out, day by day.

original.note: Pali name of the king in Jataka 541 (also spelled Nimi), tied by tradition to resolve.
